biological.citation: Loss of IRF2BPL impairs neuronal maintenance through excess Wnt signaling (PMID: 35044823)
biological.summary: IRF2BPL and its Drosophila ortholog Pits repress Wnt transcription; neuronal depletion of Pits increases wingless (wg) levels in fly brains causing axonal loss, while inhibition of Wg signaling is neuroprotective. Loss of irf2bpl in zebrafish increases wnt1 transcription and downstream signaling, and WNT1 is elevated in patient-derived astrocytes. IRF2BPL physically and genetically interacts with the Wnt antagonist CKIα to antagonize Wnt transcription and signaling.

biological.citation: Mechanisms of IRF2BPL-related disorders and identification of a potential therapeutic strategy (PMID: 36476864)
biological.summary: Patient skin fibroblasts reprogrammed to astrocytes and neurons showed that truncated IRF2BPL variants sequester wild-type protein to the cytoplasm and cause aggregation, while full-length IRF2BPL localizes to the nucleus. Patient astrocytes failed to support neuronal survival in coculture and exhibited aberrant mitochondria and respiratory dysfunction. Treatment with CuATSM rescued neuronal survival and restored mitochondrial function in vitro.

biological.citation: IRF2BPL Is Associated with Neurological Phenotypes (PMID: 30057031)
biological.summary: The Drosophila IRF2BPL ortholog pits is broadly expressed including in the nervous system; complete loss of pits is lethal early in development, whereas partial RNAi knockdown in neurons leads to neurodegeneration. IRF2BPL nonsense variants behave as severe loss-of-function alleles in flies, while missense variants produce a range of phenotypes, demonstrating a requirement for this gene in neuronal function and maintenance.

biological.citation: Forkhead Box F2 Suppresses Gastric Cancer through a Novel FOXF2-IRF2BPL-β-Catenin Signaling Axis (PMID: 29374064)
biological.summary: FOXF2 directly binds the promoter of IRF2BPL and induces its transcriptional expression; IRF2BPL in turn interacts with β-catenin, increasing its ubiquitination and degradation independently of GSK-3β. This FOXF2-IRF2BPL axis suppresses Wnt signaling and acts as a tumor suppressor in gastric cancer. IRF2BPL is thus identified as an E3 ligase that ubiquitinates β-catenin.

biological.citation: IRF2BPL inhibits proliferation, migration and invasion of osteosarcoma cells by inhibiting FOSL2-mediated PI3K/AKT pathway activation (PMID: 40834975)
biological.summary: IRF2BPL is downregulated in osteosarcoma and its overexpression suppresses cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro and in vivo, while silencing enhances these processes. Mechanistically, IRF2BPL regulates the FOSL2/PI3K/AKT/mTOR axis through ubiquitin-mediated degradation of FOSL2. A subcutaneous xenograft tumor model validated its tumor-suppressive role in vivo.

biological.citation: IRF2BPL transcriptionally regulates IGFBP2 to promote tumor progression and suppresses immune cell infiltration in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (PMID: 41413713)
biological.summary: IRF2BPL acts as a transcriptional activator (non-classical E3 ubiquitin ligase function) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma, promoting IGFBP2 transcription and facilitating malignant phenotypes both in vivo and in vitro. IRF2BPL is highly expressed in ESCC cells and its hyperactive IRF2BPL-IGFBP2 axis also inhibits immune cell infiltration in the tumor microenvironment. The chemical ONC201 effectively impeded ESCC progression driven by this axis.

biological.citation: N(6)-methyladenosine-modified circRNA RERE modulates osteoarthritis by regulating β-catenin ubiquitination and degradation (PMID: 35733354)
biological.summary: IRF2BPL functions downstream of the circRERE/miR-195-5p axis to regulate ubiquitination and degradation of β-catenin in chondrocytes, exerting chondroprotective effects in osteoarthritis. AAV-mediated knockdown of Irf2bpl in a mouse destabilization of medial meniscus model worsened OA severity, and these detrimental effects were counteracted by the β-catenin inhibitor ICG-001. This study confirms IRF2BPL's role as a regulator of β-catenin ubiquitination in a non-neurological tissue context.

biological.citation: IRF2BPL-Related Disorder, Causing Neurodevelopmental Disorder with Regression, Abnormal Movements, Loss of Speech and Seizures (NEDAMSS) Is Characterized by Pathology Consistent with DRPLA (PMID: 39224955)
biological.summary: Postmortem pathological analysis of an IRF2BPL-related disorder patient revealed findings consistent with dentatorubral-pallidoluysian atrophy (DRPLA), including polyglutamine (polyQ) inclusions, suggesting a novel disease mechanism involving the polyQ repeat tract. The IRF2BPL c.562C>T variant resulted in decreased mRNA in brain tissue and destabilization of the protein product with downstream molecular abnormalities in patient-derived cells. This is the first detailed pathological description of NEDAMSS.

biological.citation: Neurodevelopmental disorder caused by a truncating de novo variant of IRF2BPL (PMID: 33278788)
biological.summary: In cells harboring a truncating IRF2BPL mutation, the cellular localization of IRF2BPL was altered and the level of ubiquitinated proteins was significantly decreased compared to control cells, implicating impairment of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway. Bioinformatics predicted IRF2BPL association with IRF2 and 10 other genes involved in ubiquitin binding pathways. These findings support a role for IRF2BPL in ubiquitin-mediated protein degradation relevant to neurological disease.

biological.citation: Differential Retinal Protein Expression in Primary and Secondary Retinal Ganglion Cell Degeneration Identified by Integrated SWATH and Target-Based Proteomics (PMID: 34445296)
biological.summary: IRF2BPL was identified as one of six proteins regulated in both temporal and nasal retinal quadrants following localized optic nerve injury in adult Wistar rats, suggesting a role in retinal ganglion cell degeneration. Proteomic analysis using SWATH-MS and MRM-MS detected IRF2BPL expression changes in the context of primary and secondary RGC degeneration. This provides evidence for IRF2BPL expression and regulation in the retina under neurodegenerative conditions.
